correctness.rationale: For each fixed pair of symbol counts, direct enumeration of all eight triple patterns shows they depend precisely on three integer zero-prefix moments. The length-three deck determines those moments because shorter decks can be recovered by counting extensions. Two independent linear constraints leave at most one free variable for at most three ones, and the square norm intersects the line at no more than two points. At four ones a rank-two integer family has prescribed linear moments, and algebraic norm powers have constant square norm. The root-of-unity obstruction proves distinctness for every k; strict coordinate separation and padding give the all-length logarithmic lower bound. The included checker tests 2,372 short-word moment identities, the three-one upper bound through length fourteen and concrete witnesses for k=1 through 5. Finite computations are corroboration, not infinite proof.

evidence: Rigo–Salimov 2013 Proposition 2 gives a global polynomial upper bound on the number of m-binomial classes of length n; Lemma 3 gives the exact number of binary two-binomial classes.
Lejeune–Rigo–Rosenfeld 2020 Proposition 12 bounds the total number of k-binomial classes as n grows, while its concrete class-generation algorithm concerns two-binomial equivalence.
broader_coverage.reasoning: A bound for the number of distinct decks says nothing decisive about the maximum inverse-image size at exactly four ones: it may coexist with bounded or arbitrarily growing fibers. The specific two-binomial classification does not imply the weight-four three-deck result. Neither stronger-looking coverage is a covering theorem.

evidence: Chrisnata et al. Theorem 23 (attributed to Manvel et al.) proves uniqueness when weight is at most deck length minus one, and Section 5.3 studies weight three at deck length three; its definitions include zero-gap vectors and fixed-weight deck counts.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: A two-preimage bound at weight three does not imply the threshold, and a zero-gap matrix parameterization at weight three or a total class count does not yield arbitrarily large fibers at weight four. The new arithmetic argument produces k+1 pairwise distinct integral solutions at identical three-deck and is independent of those prior conclusions.

originality.rationale: The inspected complete primary works introduce the equivalence, count total deck classes or treat fixed weight three, whereas this claim proves a sharp fixed-support transition from bounded to unbounded fiber cardinalities with an explicit norm-form construction at weight four. Stronger-looking results on global class counts do not imply or state this particular fixed-support family. Priority risk remains for unindexed equivalent statements.
residual_risks: An unindexed older proof may contain a specialization yielding exactly the four-one unbounded-fiber theorem.
The 2019 short conference version was compared by its published objectives and the available full expanded 2021 version, not treated as a separately fully inspected six-page text.
The logarithmic lower bound is not asserted optimal; that limitation does not undermine its unboundedness conclusion.

value.rationale: The least number of marked symbols permitting unbounded multiplicity-sensitive three-deck reconstruction ambiguity is a natural operational threshold: at most three markers, every observation has at most two originals, while exactly four markers admits logarithmically growing ambiguity for every sufficiently large length. The explicit quadratic-form norm family provides a structural rather than ad-hoc finite mechanism. It sharpens qualitative reconstruction uncertainty in sparsely marked strings without requiring a downstream conjecture or exact global optimum.
